observation: Concept pre-locked (10 hard rules) by founder eliminated typical back-and-forth on primitive definition. No Phase 0→1 rework.

TDD red phase comprehensive — all 11 ACs had failing tests written before implementation (phase 2: test commit 754b4ab6). Zero test-writing debt at ship; upfront AC specificity prevented mid-stream scope surprises.

Architecture critique caught CRITICAL silence violation before code (hard rule #8: cost-breach bypasses factory silence but respects quiet hours). Round-1 critique flagged, round-2 approval (8/10) after revision. Saved ~4h code-review rework.

Two-lens review model effective — Phase 2 (design + architecture critique) caught structural/contract gaps; Phase 4 (code review) caught implementation slop. Neither lens alone would have caught all; together: comprehensive.

Backend implementation faithful to locked contracts — the two hardest constraints (cost-breach silence split + mandatory kind discriminator) implemented exactly as planned. @lore documentation at each decision point.

Frontend design divergence unvetted in Phase 3 — popover row redesigned from locked spec (single-line dense → two-tier stacked, hover-reveal → always-visible text buttons). Only discovered in Phase 4 code review (W1), too late to prevent ship.

Dead control introduced by AF8 — error-state Retry button (C1) rendered but had no onClick handler. Not a pre-existing AF16 issue; AF8-introduced slop. Test passed because assertion checked only presence, not functionality.

Hollow test assertions masked failures — AC10 loading-state test used `getByRole ?? querySelector` + `.toBeDefined()` on a truthy expression, which always passes. Same pattern on Retry button assertion (passed on presence, failed on function).

Stories rendered one state four times — NotificationPopover.stories.tsx: Empty/LoadingState/ErrorState/Populated all rendered identically because component hooked into real useNotifications. Stories non-deterministic, defeating purpose of state stories.
Five quality warnings all fixable in one commit — W3 (N+1 /seen loop), W4 (loose UUID validation), W5 (duplicated branches), docs gaps. Code-quality discipline lacking despite red phase.

AC1 and AC5 tested underlying functions directly instead of scheduled behavior. flushQueue and recoverStuckLeases called directly; drain interval wiring proven only by 'returns disposer without throw'. Behavior correct; AC coverage incomplete.

Builder green-phase timeout cost signal — implementation commit (e64d356e, 10:31) was ~69min after test commit (09:22). Followed by second attestation commit (ba874563) suggesting first session hit budget limit. Builder #2 resumed with fixes + attestation.

Timeline: 2 working days (June 10–11). Design (09:01) → Architecture (09:04) → Critique (09:09) → Revision (09:14) → Tests (09:22) → Implementation (10:31) → Review R1 (10:43) → 5 fix commits (1h) → Review R2 (11:33). Sequential phases, no parallel work.

Diff: 7842 insertions, 6292 deletions, 110 files changed. Large but appropriate for full-stack notification delivery (backend drain/listener/routes + frontend popover/Settings + schema + tests + docs).
Review-fix ratio efficient — 1 CRITICAL + 5 WARNINGs resolved in 5 fix commits + docs commit. All blockers resolved in one round. No third review cycle needed.
